events.title: Stabenow unseats Abraham
events.text: Debbie Stabenow defeated Spencer Abraham, the last Republican Michigan has elected to the U.S. Senate (in 1994).

events.title: Rogers to Congress
events.text: Mike Rogers, a former FBI agent and state senator, won the 8th District by 111 votes.

events.title: Gore carries Michigan
events.text: Michigan voted Democratic for president by about five points, part of a run from 1992 to 2012.

events.title: Kerry by 3.4
events.text: John Kerry carried Michigan by 3.4 points.

events.title: Obama by 16.5
events.text: Barack Obama carried Michigan by 16.5 points, the widest margin of the period.

events.title: Auto bankruptcies
events.text: General Motors and Chrysler went through bankruptcy with federal help.

events.title: Intelligence chair
events.text: Rogers became chairman of the House Intelligence Committee, serving until 2015.

events.title: Detroit files
events.text: Detroit filed for Chapter 9, the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history; it exited in December 2014.

events.title: Flint switches water
events.text: Flint switched its water source to the Flint River, setting off the Flint water crisis.

events.title: Peters elected
events.text: Gary Peters won the U.S. Senate seat now open in 2026.

events.title: Detroit health director
events.text: Abdul El-Sayed became Detroit's health director, serving until February 2017.

events.title: 10,704 votes
events.text: Donald Trump carried Michigan by 10,704 votes, the closest presidential result in any state that year.

events.title: Kent votes Republican
events.text: Kent County, around Grand Rapids, voted Republican for president by about three points.

events.title: Governor's primary
events.text: El-Sayed finished second to Gretchen Whitmer in the Democratic primary for governor.

events.title: Whitmer elected
events.text: Whitmer won the governorship with 53.3 percent.

events.title: Biden by 154,188
events.text: Joe Biden carried Michigan by 154,188 votes, 2.8 points.

events.title: Peters re-elected
events.text: Peters beat John James by 92,335 votes.

events.title: Kent flips
events.text: Kent County voted Democratic for president, by about six points.

events.title: Proposal 3
events.text: Voters wrote abortion rights into the state constitution, with 56.7 percent.

events.title: A Democratic legislature
events.text: Democrats won both chambers of the legislature, for the first time since 1983.

events.title: Wayne County health
events.text: El-Sayed became Wayne County's health director, serving until 2025.

events.title: 13 percent uncommitted
events.text: In the Democratic presidential primary, 'uncommitted' won 13.2 percent over the war in Gaza.

events.title: Dearborn shifts
events.text: Dearborn, where most residents report Middle Eastern or North African ancestry, voted for Trump (unofficial results).

events.title: Trump by 80,103
events.text: Donald Trump carried Michigan by 80,103 votes, 1.4 points.

events.title: Slotkin by 19,006
events.text: Elissa Slotkin beat Rogers for the Senate by 19,006 votes, 0.3 points, on the same ballot.

events.title: State House flips
events.text: Republicans won the state House, 58 seats to 52.

events.title: Peters retires
events.text: On 28 January Peters announced he would not seek a third term.

events.title: Auto tariffs
events.text: A 25 percent federal tariff on imported cars and light trucks was announced on 26 March.

events.title: Rogers runs again
events.text: On 14 April Rogers launched a second Senate campaign.

events.title: El-Sayed runs
events.text: El-Sayed entered the Democratic primary, endorsed by Senator Bernie Sanders.

events.title: Trump endorses Rogers
events.text: On 24 July President Trump endorsed Rogers; he faced no Republican opponent.

events.title: A data centre campus
events.text: A data-centre campus of more than one gigawatt was announced for Saline Township.

events.title: Temple Israel attack
events.text: In March a man drove a car into Temple Israel in West Bloomfield and fired at a guard.

events.title: McMorrow withdraws
events.text: On 5 July State Senator Mallory McMorrow left the Democratic primary.

events.title: Primary day
events.text: On 4 August El-Sayed beat Representative Haley Stevens by about one point.

events.title: Unity
events.text: Stevens, McMorrow, Whitmer and Peters endorsed El-Sayed after the primary.

events.title: A toss-up
events.text: In September and October forecasters rated the race from toss-up to leaning Democratic.

events.title: First debate
events.text: On 8 October El-Sayed and Rogers debated in Grand Rapids.

events.title: Record spending
events.text: Candidates, parties and outside groups had spent more than $268 million on the race by 15 October, a state record.

events.title: Second debate
events.text: On 21 October El-Sayed and Rogers met for their second and final debate, on Detroit's WXYZ-TV.

events.title: Early voting
events.text: Statewide early in-person voting runs from 24 October to 1 November.

events.title: Election Day
events.text: On 3 November Michigan chooses among six candidates for the Senate.

eras: A Democratic state, an industrial crisis
Split tickets and an open seat
chartNote: Each state is coloured by the margin of the most recent presidential popular vote (Democratic minus Republican share of all votes, from certified results). It is a simplification: Michigan elects its senator in its own race, and many Michiganders split their tickets (in 2024 Donald Trump carried Michigan by 1.4 points while Elissa Slotkin won its Senate seat by 0.3), so the presidential colour is a backdrop, not a forecast. Shares are of land area, not of people or votes. Boundaries are today's states (Natural Earth, with the Great Lakes removed); the map is framed on Michigan, so outer states are cut at the edge.
